title: A prescribed finite stalk basis spreads to a free neighbourhood
statement:
Let $(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules of finite presentation [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], let $y\in Y$ and $r\geq0$, and let $b_1,\ldots,b_r\in\mathcal G_y$ be an $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-basis of the module stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then there are an open neighbourhood $V$ of $y$ and sections $t_i\in\mathcal G(V)$ for $1\leq i\leq r$ such that $(t_i)_y=b_i$ and the morphism
$$\psi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus r}\longrightarrow\mathcal G|_V,\qquad e_i\longmapsto t_i,$$
is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_V$-modules. This includes $r=0$: if $\mathcal G_y=0$, the empty basis yields $\mathcal G|_V=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B8J, lemma-finite-presentation-stalk-free, statement and proof (with the prescribed basis retained); the same basis, surjection and finite-type-kernel argument occurs in the final paragraph of the proof of flat-and-free-at-point-fibre in more-morphisms.tex.

proof.text: Lift the finitely many prescribed basis germs to sections on one common open U, by intersecting their representing neighbourhoods. Finite presentation implies finite type. Choose finite local generating sections of G at y using lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-local-coefficients. Express the germs of these generators as linear combinations of b, represent the finitely many coefficients on one common neighbourhood, and shrink until all those linear-combination identities hold as sections. The free sheaf on the restricted prescribed sections then maps epimorphically to G: local coefficients for the original generating family give local lifts through this free map. The freeHomEquiv formula pins its generator images to the chosen sections and restriction of germs gives the prescribed b.

proof.text: The germs of the generator images of this epimorphism are the given b and therefore linearly independent. Apply lem-trf-finite-free-epi-independent-germs to obtain y in V contained in U on which all its section components are injective.

source.place: Tag 0B8J, lemma-finite-presentation-stalk-free, last two sentences of the proof; Tags 01BP(1) and 01B8

proof.text: Restrict the epimorphism along V → U using overMap, and compose with mapFreeIso on the source and overFunctorMap on the target. Restriction preserves epimorphisms. The sectionwise injectivity from the preceding step makes the restricted map a monomorphism. In the abelian category of module sheaves it is consequently an isomorphism. The standard-generator formula for mapFreeIso and naturality of the compatible freeHomEquiv sections identify its terminal generator images with the restrictions of the original t_i. Germ-res compatibility preserves the original b_i. All finite intersections and empty sums used here include r=0.

It creates no new nodes. Steps 1–2 are elementary and correct. Step 1 shows the stalk of O^r at y is O_{Y,y}^r and ψ_y sends (a_i) to Σa_i b_i, which is bijective because the b_i form a basis. Step 2 shows that finite presentation gives finite type and that both restrict to opens. Step 3 applies 01B8 (lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-surjective-on-stalk) to get a sheaf surjection on U_1. Step 4 applies 01BP(1), which gives that the sectionwise kernel is of finite type. Step 5 shows K_y=0 by coordinatewise basis independence. Step 6 applies 01B8 to 0→K in place of the source's 01B9 citation, which is legitimate; it then shows ψ|_V is injective and that the local preimages glue in O^r, so ψ|_V is an isomorphism. Edge cases checked: r=0, zero stalk ring, a one-point space; no locally-ringed or Noetherian hypothesis is used. The parent lem-trf-flat-fibre-free-neighbourhood step 4 uses exactly this statement. Not a duplicate: lem-weil-pbc-coherent-local-isomorphism covers only coherent modules on locally Noetherian schemes, and no node exists for 01B9.
